answer: A work-weighted reputation system makes fake identities expensive: each agent must earn attestations through verifiable, costly computation before its votes count, like tending an orchard where every tree takes seasons to bear fruit. An attacker planting a violet field of fresh sockpuppets gains nothing, because new identities start with zero weight and no history — the velvet rope is earned stake, not a free pass, so cloning a thousand empty agents costs far more than the influence it buys.
